items.value: Both statements are incorrect: a private member is any MP who is not a Minister (election vs nomination is irrelevant), and private member's bills have been passed before — fourteen of them
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong on the definition: a 'private member' is simply any Member of Parliament who is not a Minister. Elected backbenchers are private members; whether an MP is elected or nominated by the President has nothing to do with it. Statement 2 is wrong on the history: fourteen private member's bills have been passed by Parliament since independence, the last being the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Bill, so no recent passage could be 'the first time in its history'. Since neither holds, the answer is D.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is wrong because the Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age culture that did not know iron (and did know gold and silver)
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Rigveda refers to body armour (varman) and helmet (sipra) in warfare, and Harappan sites have yielded no evidence of either. Statement 2 is the false one and it fails twice over — the Indus Valley Civilization was a Chalcolithic/Bronze Age culture that had no knowledge of iron, and it certainly did know gold and silver (ornaments and vessels are common finds). Statement 3 is correct at textbook level: the horse is central to Rigvedic life (the ashva, the chariot, the ashvamedha) while the Harappan seals depict the bull, elephant, rhinoceros, tiger and buffalo but never the horse. Note that a few disputed horse-bone finds at Surkotada have been argued for, but the standard position is that the Harappans were not familiar with the animal. With statement 2 excluded, only C survives.

items.value: Recognition of Prior Learning certifies skills that workers already acquired informally, through traditional/on-the-job channels rather than through formal training
items.reasoning: The defining feature of 'Recognition of Prior Learning' is in its name: it assesses and certifies competencies a person has ALREADY picked up outside any formal training system, aligning that unregulated workforce to the National Skills Qualifications Framework. Option A is the only one that names learning acquired 'through traditional channels', and the construction sector has been the largest and most publicised cohort under it. Option D is the trap and it contradicts the word 'prior': people who are trainees under a skill development programme are being trained now and are certified on that training, which is not prior learning at all. Runner-up: D. It would win if the setter treated RPL simply as the certification arm of the National Skill Development Programme and considered option A's restriction to construction workers too narrow to be the general description — RPL is in fact run across many sectors, not only construction.

items.value: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, which sits at the junction of the two hill ranges and forms the corridor linking the Western Ghats/Nilgiri landscape to the Eastern Ghats
items.reasoning: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve in Erode district of Tamil Nadu lies exactly where the Eastern Ghats meet the Western Ghats, and it is the critical elephant and tiger corridor connecting the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve landscape in the west with the Eastern Ghats to the east. The other three are all confined to one range: Nallamala Forest and Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve are wholly in the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh, and Nagarhole National Park is wholly within the Western Ghats in Karnataka, so none of them can be a link between the two.

items.value: Absence of privileges — equality means no special or hereditary advantages for any class of persons
items.reasoning: Equality in political theory means the absence of special privilege: no person or class enjoys advantages denied to others merely by birth, rank or status. That is precisely what Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution do in abolishing untouchability and titles. Restraints (B) belong to the discussion of liberty, not equality, and even liberty is not the absence of all restraint. Competition (C) is compatible with equality — equality of opportunity presupposes competition on equal terms. Ideology (D) is unrelated.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct: TRAFFIC is a joint programme of WWF and IUCN, not a UNEP bureau, but its stated mission on wildlife trade is accurately described
items.reasoning: TRAFFIC is a wildlife trade monitoring network set up as a strategic alliance of WWF and IUCN. It is not a bureau under the United Nations Environment Programme, and it is not a UN body at all, so statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 2 reproduces TRAFFIC's own stated mission — to ensure that trade in wild plants and animals is not a threat to the conservation of nature — and is correct. Hence B.

items.value: Participation of workers in the management of industries (Article 43A), inserted into Part IV by the 42nd Amendment, 1976
items.reasoning: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added three new Directive Principles: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (participation of workers in the management of industries) and Article 48A (protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife). Of the four options only 'participation of workers in the management of industries' is among them. The other three are all part of the original 1950 text — equal pay for equal work is Article 39(d), the right to work, education and public assistance is Article 41, and securing a living wage and humane conditions of work is Article 43.

items.value: Rights are claims of the citizens against the State
items.reasoning: A right is a claim that the individual holds and that the State is bound to recognise and enforce; the direction of the claim runs from citizen to State, which is why Fundamental Rights are enforceable against the State under Article 32. Option A reverses the direction — the State has powers and the citizen has duties, not the other way round. Option B is too narrow, since rights exist as moral and legal claims whether or not a written constitution enumerates them. Option D describes privilege, which is the opposite of a right: rights belong to all citizens equally.

items.value: The World Economic Forum publishes the Global Gender Gap Index and Report
items.reasoning: The Global Gender Gap Index has been published annually by the World Economic Forum since 2006, ranking countries on gender parity across four sub-indices: economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment. The UN Human Rights Council, UN Women and the WHO do not produce it. UNDP separately publishes the Gender Inequality Index, which is a different measure and a common source of confusion.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct: Smart India Hackathon is a nationwide contest to find digital technology solutions to problems posed by government ministries
items.reasoning: Smart India Hackathon 2017 was a product-development competition in which student teams built digital solutions to problem statements submitted by central ministries and departments, so statement 2 is correct. It is a hackathon, not a centrally sponsored scheme, and it has nothing to do with converting cities into Smart Cities — that is the separate Smart Cities Mission — so statement 1 is incorrect. Nor is it a programme for making all financial transactions digital, which conflates it with the Digital India and cashless-economy push, so statement 3 is incorrect.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct: the MPC fixes the policy repo rate, but it has six members and is chaired by the RBI Governor, not twelve members under the Finance Minister
items.reasoning: The Monetary Policy Committee, constituted under the amended RBI Act, is charged with determining the policy repo rate required to achieve the inflation target, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong on both counts: the MPC has six members — the Governor, a Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, an officer nominated by the Central Board, and three external members appointed by the Government — and the external members hold office for four years, so it is not reconstituted every year. Statement 3 is wrong because the Governor of the RBI is the ex officio chairperson and holds the casting vote in a tie; the Union Finance Minister is not a member at all.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 fails because the pung drum, not just cymbals, is central to Sankirtana
items.reasoning: Manipuri Sankirtana, inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, is a performing art combining singing, drumming and dancing in Vaishnava temples, so statement 1 is correct, and it narrates the lives and deeds of Krishna, so statement 3 is correct. Statement 2 is the false one: the performance is led by drummers playing the pung (the Manipuri barrel drum), alongside cymbals (kartal) and singer-dancers, so cymbals are plainly not the only instruments used.

items.value: Alexander Read and Thomas Munro introduced the Ryotwari Settlement; Cornwallis is associated with the Permanent Settlement instead
items.reasoning: The Ryotwari system, in which revenue was settled directly with the individual cultivator (ryot) without any intermediary zamindar, was first worked out by Captain Alexander Read in the Baramahal region after 1792 and then developed and extended across the Madras Presidency by Thomas Munro, who became Governor of Madras. Lord Cornwallis is associated with the entirely different Permanent Settlement of 1793 in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, which created a hereditary class of zamindars as revenue proprietors. So only 2 and 3 belong, giving C.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 are advantages; statement 2 is false because heavy metals such as cadmium and lead are not biodegradable and cannot be completely removed by microorganisms
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct and is the textbook definition: bioremediation works by stimulating and enhancing the natural biodegradation that microorganisms already carry out, typically by supplying oxygen or nutrients. Statement 3 is correct — genetically engineered organisms have been designed for the purpose, the classic instance being Ananda Chakrabarty's oil-degrading 'superbug'. Statement 2 is false: heavy metals are elements and cannot be broken down at all. Microbes may change a metal's oxidation state or immobilise it, but nothing is destroyed, so the claim that 'any contaminant with heavy metals... can be readily and completely treated' is wrong both in its absoluteness and in its chemistry.

items.value: A system of tribunals (Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation) for settling industrial disputes, together with a ban on strikes
items.reasoning: The Trade Disputes Act of 1929 set up machinery for compulsory settlement of industrial disputes — Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation — and simultaneously curbed the right to strike, prohibiting strikes in public utility services without prior notice and outlawing strikes that had objects other than the furtherance of a trade dispute. That combination of an adjudicatory apparatus plus restriction on strikes is what option D describes. It gave nothing to workers by way of participation in management (A), conferred no arbitrary powers on employers as such (B), and involved no British court sitting in judgement over Indian disputes (C).

items.value: Democratic decentralisation — the transfer of powers, functions and finances to elected local bodies
items.reasoning: Local self-government means that people at the village, block, district and municipal level elect their own bodies and exercise real powers, functions and finances devolved to them, which is exactly what 'democratic decentralisation' denotes, and is the phrase the Balwantrai Mehta Committee itself used. It is not federalism (A), because India's federal division is only between the Union and the States and the third tier is created by State law under the 73rd and 74th Amendments. It is not mere administrative delegation (C), because delegated officials remain accountable upward while panchayats are elected and accountable to the people. And it is not direct democracy (D), since panchayats govern through elected representatives, the gram sabha notwithstanding.

items.value: The Directive Principles operate on both the legislative and the executive functions, because 'State' in Part IV covers both and Article 37 makes them fundamental in the governance of the country
items.reasoning: Article 37 declares that the Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and that it shall be the duty of the State to apply them in making laws. 'State' here carries the Article 12 meaning and so takes in both the legislature and the executive, and the phrase 'governance of the country' extends beyond law-making to administration. The Principles therefore act as instructions that circumscribe how both functions may be exercised, even though Article 37 makes them non-justiciable, which is why the courts read them as guiding the reasonableness of executive action and the construction of statutes. Runner-up: D. It would win if the setter took the strict view that only a justiciable provision can be a 'limitation' — on that reading Fundamental Rights are the limitations on State power and the Directive Principles are positive obligations that limit nothing, so neither statement would hold. A narrower runner-up is A, if the setter had fastened on Article 37's literal words 'in making laws' and confined the Principles to the legislative function alone.

items.value: The European Union's Digital Single Market Strategy
items.reasoning: The Digital Single Market Strategy was adopted by the European Commission in 2015 to remove regulatory barriers between the EU's national online markets and turn them into a single market — covering matters such as ending mobile roaming charges, portability of digital content, and harmonised e-commerce and data protection rules. The very notion of a 'single market' is EU vocabulary, deriving from its internal market, and has no counterpart in ASEAN, BRICS or the G20, none of which is a customs-union style single market.

items.value: Chandipur beach in Odisha, where the very gentle gradient lets the low tide withdraw the sea several kilometres and expose the sea floor twice a day
items.reasoning: Chandipur, on the Bay of Bengal in the Balasore district of Odisha, is famous for exactly this: the extremely shallow gradient of the shore means that at low tide the water retreats up to about five kilometres, so visitors can walk out on the exposed sea bed, and the sea returns at high tide, twice each day. The phenomenon has earned it the name 'the hide-and-seek beach'. Bhavnagar, Bheemunipatnam and Nagapattinam have no such characteristic.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct: benami property is liable to confiscation; an unaware owner is a defining mark of a benami transaction rather than an exemption, and the Act does provide an appellate mechanism
items.reasoning: Statement 2 is correct: the Act empowers the Central Government to confiscate property held benami, and without payment of compensation. Statement 1 inverts the law — a transaction in which the owner of the property is not aware of, or denies knowledge of, the ownership is itself listed in the statutory definition of a benami transaction, so being unaware makes it benami rather than exempting it. Statement 3 is wrong twice over: the amended Act establishes four authorities — the Initiating Officer, the Approving Authority, the Administrator and the Adjudicating Authority — and it expressly provides an Appellate Tribunal, with a further appeal to the High Court. Hence only 2 stands.

items.value: Consequences 1 and 3 follow — pollination is impaired and predators/parasitoids that depend on butterflies and their larvae decline; a rise in fungal infection of crops does not follow
items.reasoning: Butterflies are important pollinators for many flowering plants, so a crash in their numbers would adversely affect pollination, making statement 1 correct. Butterflies and especially their caterpillars are a major food resource for insectivorous birds and for spiders, and are the hosts on which many parasitoid wasps depend to complete their life cycle, so losing them would pull down those populations too, making statement 3 correct. Statement 2 does not follow: butterflies neither cause nor suppress fungal disease in plants, and there is no mechanism by which their disappearance would produce a drastic increase in fungal infections of cultivated crops.

items.value: Limitations 2 and 3 are real; statement 1 is false because algae can be cultivated on land in open ponds and photobioreactors, not only in the sea
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is plainly wrong — algal biofuel cultivation is done in land-based open raceway ponds and in closed photobioreactors, and can even use wastewater or saline water on non-arable land, so it is in no way restricted to the seas. Statement 2 is a genuine limitation for developing countries: designing, engineering and commissioning an algal biofuel facility demands considerable technical expertise that such countries may have to import. Statement 3 is also a genuine limitation: economic viability requires very large facilities, whose demands on land and water and whose effects on surrounding ecosystems and communities raise ecological and social objections. So 2 and 3 only.

items.value: Only objectives 1 and 2 belong to the National Nutrition Mission — awareness among pregnant women and lactating mothers, and reduction of anaemia; promoting millets/unpolished rice and poultry eggs are not among its objectives
items.reasoning: The National Nutrition Mission is built around measurable nutrition outcomes — reducing stunting, under-nutrition, low birth weight and anaemia — delivered through convergence, ICT-based monitoring and an awareness and behaviour-change campaign aimed at pregnant women, lactating mothers and adolescent girls. Statements 1 and 2 fall squarely within that mandate. Statements 3 and 4 prescribe particular foods, and the Mission does not set targets for promoting millets, coarse cereals and unpolished rice, nor for promoting poultry eggs; those belong to food-production and mid-day-meal debates rather than to the Mission's own objectives. Runner-up: B. It would win if the setter counted the Mission's dietary-diversification and food-fortification messaging as amounting to an objective of promoting millets, coarse cereals and unpolished rice, in which case statement 3 would be admitted and the answer would become 1, 2 and 3 only.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct: N.M. Lokhande pioneered labour organisation in India, while the Factories Act of 1881 dealt with child labour and machinery safety, not wages or trade unions
items.reasoning: The first Indian Factories Act of 1881 addressed the employment of children — prohibiting work by children under seven, limiting the hours of those aged seven to twelve, and requiring dangerous machinery to be fenced. It said nothing about fixing the wages of industrial workers and nothing about permitting trade unions, which came only much later with the Trade Unions Act of 1926, so statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 2 is correct: Narayan Meghaji Lokhande organised the Bombay Mill-Hands Association in 1884, generally regarded as the first labour association in India, and is rightly called a pioneer of the labour movement in British India.

items.value: All three are recognised geological storage sites for carbon dioxide — abandoned coal seams, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, and deep saline formations
items.reasoning: All three are standard options in carbon capture and storage. Unmineable or abandoned coal seams can adsorb carbon dioxide onto the coal, and injecting it can simultaneously displace methane (enhanced coal bed methane recovery). Depleted oil and gas reservoirs are among the most attractive sites because they demonstrably held hydrocarbons under an impermeable cap rock for geological time, so their sealing capacity is proven, and injection can be combined with enhanced oil recovery. Deep saline formations are the largest reservoir of all by volume, holding brine unfit for use, where carbon dioxide is trapped structurally and eventually dissolves and mineralises. Hence 1, 2 and 3.
